analysis.note: The neuter -am form is formally nominative/accusative; here it is taken as nominative, agreeing with cittam. Internally vītarāga is understood in the usual sense ‘one whose rāga has gone, passionless’; Vyāsa specifies the object as the citta/ālambana of such a person.

verification.detail: compound stem vītarāgaviṣaya as Napumsaka/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Disjunctive: ‘or’, marking another alternative means of settling the mind.
Formally ambiguous with accusative singular, but read as nominative subject by the bhāṣya: the yogin’s mind attains steadiness.

justifications.decision: The sūtra compound is not merely ‘a passionless object’ nor ‘an object belonging to a passionless person’; Vyāsa takes the yogin’s citta to be colored by the ālambana consisting of vītarāga-citta. Thus viṣaya is read as meditative object/support, and the whole compound is an adjective of cittam.
options_considered: an object belonging to a vītarāga
the mind as object for a vītarāga
the yogin’s mind having vītarāga-citta as its object/support
justifications.chosen: vītarāgaviṣayaṃ = ‘whose object/support is the mind of one free from rāga’

evidence.quote: vītarāgacittālambanoparaktaṃ vā yoginaś cittaṃ sthitipadaṃ labhata iti.
evidence.translation: Or, the yogin’s mind, tinged by the support consisting of the mind of one free from rāga, attains the state of steadiness. The printed labhata is taken as the expected labhate.

justifications.decision: Although cittam is formally also accusative, the bhāṣya explicitly construes yoginaś cittaṃ as what attains sthitipada. Therefore the sūtra is elliptical: ‘the mind [becomes steady/attains steadiness]’, not an instruction with cittam as an object such as ‘meditate on the mind’.
options_considered: accusative object of an implied injunction
nominative subject of the implied stabilization-result
justifications.chosen: cittam is nominative singular, the subject of the implied result

evidence.translation: The yogin’s mind attains the state of steadiness; labhata is printed, probably for labhate.

justifications.decision: The bhāṣya repeats vā in its paraphrase, so the particle continues the series of optional supports for stabilizing the mind.

evidence.translation: Or, tinged by the support of the mind of one free from rāga.

justifications.decision: In vītarāga, rāga is taken in its affective yogic sense, so vītarāga means ‘free from attachment/passion’, not simply ‘devoid of color/redness’. The commentary repeats the technical compound but does not define rāga here, so this decision rests on grammar and standard yogic usage rather than a fresh gloss in this line.

translation: Or [steadiness comes for] the mind whose object is the mind of one free from attachment (vītarāga).
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might render vītarāgaviṣayam as ‘a passionless object’ or ‘an object of the passionless’; Vyāsa instead identifies the object/support as the mind of a vītarāga.
It might take cittam as an accusative object of an implied practice-command. Vyāsa construes the yogin’s citta as the subject that attains steadiness.
It might leave viṣaya vague as ‘sphere’ or ‘domain’; the bhāṣya narrows it to ālambana, a meditative support/object.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 segmented vītarāgaviṣayam as vīta + rāga + viṣayam and treated viṣayam as the simple stem viṣaya. I treat the full surface as one inflected compound stem vītarāgaviṣaya, because Vyāsa glosses the sūtra phrase by the compound vītarāgacittālambanoparaktam in line 1.

ByT5’s internal tag vīta_vī_PaCp is not adopted as a separate word-analysis. Within vītarāga, vīta is the conventional participial element ‘gone away/departed’ in the sense ‘whose rāga has departed’; the sūtra-word as a whole is a nominal compound.
open_questions: The commentary line prints labhata; syntactically and idiomatically labhate is expected. I have quoted labhata verbatim but interpreted the sentence accordingly.
commentary_lines: vītarāgacittālambanoparaktaṃ vā yoginaś cittaṃ sthitipadaṃ labhata iti.
